statements.venue: Remarks at Virginia State University presenting federal funding for an AI and cybersecurity center, published on her official site
statements.quote: Just like any tool, AI can be used for good, but it can also be used for bad. This Center is to ensure that all of the policies, legal, and ethical frameworks that have governed human interactions also govern AI, and that human beings control AI, not the other way around.
statements.context: She presented $1.03 million in community project funding for a Center for Generative AI and Industrial Cybersecurity at Virginia State University, which the release says will study AI risks such as misinformation, copyright, bias and jobs.
statements.reason: Saying humans must control AI 'not the other way around' acknowledges, in general terms, a risk of AI escaping human control, but names no catastrophic harm; it could also be read as a generic D remark, so it is marked boundary.

record: Secured $1.03 million in community project funding for a Center for Generative AI and Industrial Cybersecurity at Virginia State University.

Introduced H.R. 7783, the AI-Ready Networks Act, with Rep. Jay Obernolte, asking the National Telecommunications and Information Administration for a report on integrating AI into commercial telecommunications networks.

notes: All seven web searches ran this time (six required plus one on the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act).
